title: Freshwater wetland ecosystem collapse
bottleneck: Inland wetlands are disappearing three times faster than forests, drained for agriculture and starved of water by upstream extraction, yet their collapse dynamics are poorly studied: thresholds where a wetland flips from carbon sink to source, or from nursery to dead zone, are unmapped for most systems. Groundwater-surface water interactions that sustain wetlands are invisible to current monitoring, and restoration often fails because the hydrology cannot be rebuilt.
why_it_blocks: Wetlands provide water purification, flood control, and biodiversity disproportionate to their area; their loss amplifies both floods and droughts for downstream communities. The science gap means collapses are noticed only after they are irreversible.
current_state: The Ramsar Convention tracks designated sites, but most wetlands are undesignated and unmonitored. Restoration science is advancing where hydrology is understood, yet the global trend remains rapid net loss.
